{"path": "README.md", "sha256": "aadbc841dfbc29c02eddcdadbc5bd4fd3d1b1d56572a79d88d1777975d0ed1a6", "total_lines": 405, "content": "186: Note that previous measurements included the initialization of their input,
187: which dramatically increased timings especially for small inputs.
188: 
189: ## CPU requirements
190: 
191: SipTreeHash(13) requires an AVX2-capable CPU (e.g. Haswell). HighwayHash
192: includes a dispatcher that chooses the implementation (AVX2, SSE4.1, VSX or
193: portable)  at runtime, as well as a directly callable function template that can
194: only run on the CPU for which it was built. SipHash(13) and
195: ScalarSipTreeHash(13) have no particular CPU requirements.
196: 
197: ### AVX2 vs SSE4
198: 
199: When both AVX2 and SSE4 are available, the decision whether to use AVX2 is
200: non-obvious. AVX2 vectors are twice as wide, but require a higher power license
201: (integer multiplications count as 'heavy' instructions) and can thus reduce the
202: clock frequency of the core or entire socket(!) on Haswell systems. This
203: partially explains the observed 1.25x (not 2x) speedup over SSE4. Moreover, it
204: is inadvisable to only sporadically

8: ## Quick Start

14: ensure the implementations return known-good values for a given set of inputs.

25:

27:

30:     using namespace highwayha
